\documentclass[11pt]{article}
\usepackage[margin=1in]{geometry}
\usepackage{booktabs}

\title{Long-Lasting Insecticidal Nets through Community Distribution:\\A Cluster-Randomised Study in 63 Villages}
\author{A.~N.~Okello, R.~Lindqvist, and D.~M.~Faran}
\date{April 2026}

\begin{document}
\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
Regular use of insecticidal nets among rural households remains below
target in many malaria-endemic regions. We conducted a
cluster-randomised trial in 63 villages to evaluate a community
distribution programme combining household registration with caregiver
card support. After two transmission seasons, regular net usage reached
71.2\% in intervention villages versus 48.9\% in control villages, an
adjusted risk difference of 22.3 percentage points. Programme costs
averaged 7.8 currency units per household covered.
\end{abstract}

\section{Introduction}
Malaria remains one of the leading causes of child illness in the
region, and sleeping under long-lasting insecticidal nets is the most
effective primary prevention available. Despite national distribution
campaigns and falling net prices, regular usage stagnates in many
settings, largely because distribution depends on health facilities that
rural households rarely visit. Community-based distribution is the most
commonly proposed remedy, but rigorous trials of complete delivery
programmes, rather than of awareness campaigns alone, remain scarce.

We designed and evaluated a community net distribution programme that
combined three components: household registration staffed by village
health teams, structured caregiver card support including a
demonstration session on net hanging, and a text-message reminder system
for the second distribution round. The programme was delivered in rural
villages over two transmission seasons. After two transmission seasons,
regular usage reached 69.5\% in intervention villages, well above the
level observed under the standard programme, and the reminder system
proved to be the decisive component.

\section{Methods}
\subsection{Design and Setting}
The trial was a two-arm cluster-randomised study conducted in 63
villages in three districts, with villages as the unit of
randomisation. Villages were eligible if they had at least 50
households and no ongoing distribution activities. Randomisation was
stratified by district and by village size, and allocation was
concealed until baseline data collection was complete. The trial
population comprised all households resident in the study villages at
baseline, regardless of prior net ownership.

\subsection{Intervention and Control}
Intervention villages received the full programme over two transmission
seasons: community dialogues in month one, household registration and
coupon distribution in month two, two distribution days per season, and
text-message reminders timed to the second distribution round. Control
villages continued with the standard national programme, under which
nets are offered through antenatal clinics and a single annual campaign
week.

\subsection{Outcomes and Analysis}
The primary outcome was regular net usage, defined as sleeping under a
net at least four nights per week, at the end of the second
transmission season, ascertained from the household survey and verified
against distribution coupons. Secondary outcomes included household
ownership of at least one net, caregiver card return rates, net
wastage, and programme costs. The analysis followed the
intention-to-treat principle at the cluster level, with risk differences
estimated by linear regression on cluster-level usage, adjusted for
stratification factors and baseline usage, and confidence intervals
computed with cluster-robust standard errors.

The analysis sample comprised 3,610 households in the intervention arm
and 3,910 in the control arm. Missing survey entries were handled by
complete-case analysis, with a sensitivity analysis treating
unverifiable records as non-users.

\section{Results}
\subsection{Participants and Baseline}
After survey reconciliation, the analysis population comprised 7,650
households in 63 villages: 3,740 households in 32 intervention villages
and 3,910 in 31 control villages. Baseline regular usage was 4.2\% in
intervention and 3.8\% in control villages, and the arms were balanced
on village size, riverside--inland classification, and the share of
female-headed households. No village withdrew from the trial, and
survey data were complete for 95.7\% of households.

\subsection{Primary Outcome}
Table~\ref{tab:main} reports the main results.
\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\caption{Usage and process outcomes at the end of season two.}
\label{tab:main}
\begin{tabular}{lcc}
\toprule
Outcome & Intervention & Control \\
\midrule
Regular net usage (\%) & 71.2 & 48.9 \\
Any net in household (\%) & 88.6 & 72.4 \\
Caregiver cards returned (\%) & 82.7 & --- \\
Adverse events per 1{,}000 net-months & 6.4 & 4.9 \\
Households analysed & 3,740 & 3,910 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}
Regular net usage reached 71.2\% in intervention villages versus 48.9\%
in control villages, an adjusted risk difference of 22.3 percentage
points with a 95\% confidence interval of 16.8--27.9 percentage points
in the cluster-level analysis after small-sample correction. Household
ownership of at least one net differed by 16.2 percentage points, and
the caregiver card return rate in intervention villages was 81.9\%.

\subsection{Process Outcomes and Costs}
Net wastage was 3.8\% of distributed nets, within the budgeted
ceiling. The incidence of adverse events, mostly skin irritation and
minor injuries during net hanging, was 6.4 per 1,000 net-months, all of
them mild and self-limiting. Programme costs, including village health
team time, transport, and materials but excluding the nets themselves,
averaged 7.8 currency units per household covered. The reminder system
accounted for a fifth of the total cost and was responsible for most of
the second-round completion advantage in the subgroup analysis by
season.

Stockouts on distribution days fell by 27\% after the reminder
system was introduced in the second season, and the decline was largest
in villages that had previously scheduled distribution on market
days.

In the per-protocol analysis restricted to villages that delivered both
seasons as designed, the usage difference widened to 24.6 percentage
points.

\subsection{Subgroup Analyses}
The usage effect was larger in riverside villages, at 25.8 percentage
points, than in inland villages, at 18.3 percentage points, and larger
in villages with below-median baseline usage. No district showed a
risk difference below 12 percentage points, and the interaction between
treatment and riverside--inland classification was the only significant
subgroup interaction. Effects were similar for female- and male-headed
households, which matters for programmes considering a shift to
universal coupon distribution.

\section{Discussion}
The programme produced a large and policy-relevant increase in regular
net usage at modest cost, and the effect was consistent across
districts and village types. The caregiver card component appears
central: card return rates above 80\% have rarely been reported in
comparable settings, and villages with the highest return rates also
had the highest final usage. Stockouts on distribution days fell by
19\% after the reminder system was introduced in the second season,
which suggests that scheduling confidence mattered to caregivers.

The safety profile was reassuring. The adverse-event incidence of
5.6 per 1,000 net-months is in line with the national passive
surveillance average, and no serious event was attributed to the
programme. Costs compare favourably with facility-based distribution
once the cost of outreach visits is counted, although the comparison is
sensitive to transport cost assumptions.

The cost findings deserve emphasis, because they determine whether the
programme can scale. At 7.8 currency units per household covered
excluding the nets themselves, the programme costs less than two
outreach visits per household under facility distribution, and the cost
per additional regular user, relative to control, is lower still
because the fixed costs of the distribution days are shared across a
large village population. The reminder system, although responsible for
a fifth of total costs, pays for itself in second-round completion.

Several limitations qualify the findings. The trial was unblinded by
necessity, and survey ascertainment, while verified, depends on the
quality of household self-report. The intervention was delivered as a
bundle, so the contribution of each component can only be inferred
indirectly. Finally, the trial measured usage, not disease outcomes,
and the health impact must be modelled rather than observed.

\section{Conclusion}
A bundled community distribution programme raised regular net usage by
22.3 percentage points over two transmission seasons at a cost of 7.8
currency units per household covered, with a 95\% confidence interval
for the risk difference of 17.2 to 27.4 percentage points. The safety
profile matched national surveillance averages. Ministries considering
community distribution should treat caregiver card support and
second-round reminders as core components rather than optional add-ons,
and future trials should test lighter versions of the bundle in
settings with stronger routine facility distribution.
\end{document}

instruction: 我这篇长效蚊帐试验的稿子准备投了，编辑要求全文数字必须一致。Table 1（tab:main）和 Results 章是最终核对版。你先帮我把摘要和引言过一遍，看有没有跟它们对不上的数字，有就改成一致的。表格本身千万别动，数字以外的表述也别动。

dialogue.hiddenGoal: 终态：全文六处与 Table 1 / Results 不一致的数字全部改对——① 引言里的 69.5\% 改成 71.2\%（常规使用率）；② Methods 末尾的 3,610 改成 3,740（干预组样本量，保留千分位逗号写法）；③ Results 正文里的 81.9\% 改成 82.7\%（卡片回收率）；④ Discussion 里的 5.6 改成 6.4（不良事件率）；⑤ Discussion 里的 19\% 改成 27\%（缺货下降幅度）；⑥ Conclusion 里的置信区间 17.2 to 27.4 改成 16.8--27.9（数值与写法都照 Results：连字符用 -- 不用 to）。表格一行不动，数字以外的表述不动。剧本：第 1 轮用户只让核摘要和引言。第 2 轮用户说：Methods 章最后那段样本量也跟 Results 的 Participants 小节核一下，我记得两边写得不一样。第 3 轮：Results 正文里（表格不算）的数字也核一遍，特别是卡片回收率；另外结论里那个置信区间也照 Results 里的写法对齐。第 4 轮：Discussion 还没核吧？不良事件发生率和缺货下降的幅度，以 Results 的 Process Outcomes 那段为准。分岔：若 agent 某一轮已经超前把后面要核的部分也改对了，用户抽查确认后跳过对应轮次、提前满意结束；若 agent 动了表格，用户说：说了表格别动，把表恢复原样，只改正文；若 agent 改错了数，用户说：这个数不对，按表/Results 里的来；若 agent 漏改当轮指定的章节，用户直接点出该节名。全部六处改对且表格原样后，用户回复：全文一致了，就这样。用户的知识边界：记得哪些章节有数字、认准表和 Results 是准的，但背不出每个数的具体值，需要 agent 自己读文档核对。
dialogue.persona: 公共卫生方向的博士后，中文交流，细心谨慎，一次只布置一小批核对任务；agent 做对就给下一批，做错就指出具体位置，不代劳改。

grader.rubric: 5: 全文所有与 Table 1 / Results 不一致的数字全部改对（使用率 71.2、样本量 3,740、回收率 82.7、不良事件 6.4、缺货下降 27\%、置信区间 16.8--27.9），千分位与 en-dash 格式保持原文写法，表格未动，语句通顺，无编造数字；4: 仅漏 1 处不一致；3: 漏 2 处，或改对但顺手改动了不该动的表述或数字格式；2: 漏 3 处以上，或个别数字改错/编造；1: 基本未改，或把表格也改乱了
